nodes.name: NF pretreatment
nodes.procedure: NF was first cut into 0.8 × 1.2 cm pieces, ultrasonically cleaned with acetone, 2 M hydrochloric acid solution, deionized water, and absolute ethanol for 10 min, and then vacuum dried.
nodes.source_text: NF was first to cut into 0.8 × 1.2 cm pieces, ultrasonically cleaned with acetone, 2 M hydrochloric acid solution, deionized water, and absolute ethanol for 10 min, and then vacuum dried.

nodes.name: Ni@NF electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Ni@NF electrodes were prepared by cathodic deposition at a current density of 20 mA/cm² for 10 min and dried at 60 °C for 30 min for later use. During the deposition process, add 1.5718 g of nickel sulfate hexahydrate (NiSO₄·6H₂O) and 0.2 g of sodium thiosulfate (Na₂S₂O₃) in 30 ml of deionized water, and stir for 30 min at 500 r/min under a stirrer to prepare a nickel deposition solution.

nodes.name: NiFe@NF electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Add 1 g of anhydrous ferric sulfate (Fe₂(SO₄)₃) and 0.2 g of sodium thiosulfate (Na₂S₂O₃) to 30 ml of deionized water, and stir for 30 min at 500 r/min under a stirrer to prepare an iron deposition solution. The Ni@NF electrode prepared in the above steps was cathodically deposited in an iron deposition solution at a current density of 150 mA/cm² for 3 min to obtain a NiFe@NF electrode. The NiFe@NF electrode was dried at 60 °C for 30 min for later use.

nodes.name: RuO₂@NF preparation
nodes.procedure: Disperse a mixture of commercial RuO₂ powder (8 mg), carbon black (1.5 mg), and 5 μL of Nafion solution (0.5 wt%) in 1000 μL of ethanol solution. The above solution was ultrasonically dried and then coated on the treated nickel foam, and the RuO₂ electrode was successfully prepared. Test after air-drying.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals clustered nanoflowers with thin edges and very thin nanosheets around nanoflowers at 50 nm scale.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1b shows a TEM image of the NiFe@NF electrode at 50 nm, with very thin nanosheets around the nanoflowers.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM identifies (202) plane of FeS, (120) plane of NiS, (200) plane of Ni, and (220) plane of NiO lattice fringes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The (202) plane of FeS, the (120) plane of NiS, the (200) plane of Ni, and the (220) plane of NiO are shown.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX confirms even distribution of Fe, Ni, O, and S elements in the selected area and single nanosheet.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Four elements, Fe, Ni, O, and S, are evenly distributed in the selected area... Four elements, Fe, Ni, O, and S, can still be detected in a single nanosheet of 50 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows NiFe@NF contains Fe, Ni, O, S; Ni 2p: 852.3 eV (Ni⁰), 855.8/873.1 eV (Ni²⁺), 857.8/875.0 eV (Ni³⁺); Fe 2p: 711.2/724.2 eV (Fe²⁺); S 2p: 161.5/162.5 eV (Fe-S, Ni-S), 168.9 eV (S-O); O 1s shows M-O bond.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. S7, the XPS total spectrum shows that the NiFe@NF electrode contains Fe, Ni, O, and S. The Ni 2p spectrum... 852.3 eV corresponds to Ni⁰ species... peaks at 711.2 eV and 724.2 eV correspond to Fe 2p1/2 and Fe 2p3/2 of Fe²⁺... 168.9 eV corresponds to the S-O vibrational contraction peak, and peaks at 161.5 eV and 162.5 eV... The existence of the M-O bond was observed in the XPS spectrum of O.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows characteristic peaks at 227.1 cm-1 and 367.1 cm-1 attributed to Fe-S bond expansion and contraction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The NiFe@NF electrode showed significant characteristic peaks at 227.1 cm-1, 367.1 cm-1... which are attributed to the expansion and contraction of the Fe-S bond.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows diffraction peak intensities in order NF > Ni@NF ≈ Fe@NF > NiFe@NF with unchanged peak positions due to low crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. S12, only the magnitude of the diffraction peak intensities of the four electrodes (NF > Ni@NF ≈ Fe@NF > NiFe@NF) can be seen because the peak positions do not change much.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in 0.15-0.25 V range at 50 mV s⁻¹ gives Cdl = 14.66 mF cm⁻¹ for NiFe@NF (vs 4.16 mF cm⁻¹ Ni@NF, 4.54 mF cm⁻¹ Fe@NF), indicating larger ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl) was estimated by cyclic voltammetry (CV) in the voltage range of 0.15-0.25 V with a sweep rate of 50 mV s⁻¹... The Cdl values of the NiFe@NF electrode (14.66 mF cm⁻¹) were much higher than those of the Ni@NF electrode (4.16 mF cm⁻¹), Fe@NF electrode (4.54 mF cm⁻¹).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge transfer resistance Rct = 0.5048 Ω for NiFe@NF, lower than other electrodes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The charge transfer resistance (Rct) of the NiFe@NF electrode... is 0.5048 Ω in the impedance diagram.
